question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
The outcome of the survey was a critical intervention to the questionaire prepared by Suraj and his committee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. questionaire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "questionaire" is incorrectly spelt in the given sentence; the correct spelling is "questionnaire" — a set of printed or written questions used to gather information from a number of people.
◦ Example: Every employee was asked to fill out a short questionnaire about workplace satisfaction.

• Spelling key: QUESTION + N + AIRE. The word is formed from "question" plus the French suffix "-naire", so the letter "n" is doubled before "-aire". Remembering this double "n" is the key to spelling it correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "committee" is correctly spelt — note the double "m" and the double "t".

• Option 3: "intervention" is correctly spelt — formed from "inter-" + "vention" (from the Latin venire, meaning "to come").

• Option 4: "outcome" is correctly spelt — a straightforward compound of "out" + "come".

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt double-letter words frequently asked in SSC exams: millennium, occurrence, embarrass, accommodate, recommend and questionnaire.

• Words borrowed from French ending in "-aire" (questionnaire, millionaire, solitaire) often trip up spellers on the preceding consonant — always check carefully whether it should be single or double.

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
A terrible disaster was witnessed by our country.
option_1: Our country had witnessed a terrible disaster.
option_2: Our country is witnessing a terrible disaster.
option_3: Our country witnessed a terrible disaster.
option_4: Our country witnesses a terrible disaster.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Our country witnessed a terrible disaster.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "A terrible disaster was witnessed by our country" is in the Simple Past Tense, Passive Voice.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "our country" becomes the subject; the past participle "witnessed" is converted to its simple past form "witnessed" (same form, as "witness" is a regular verb); and the subject "a terrible disaster" becomes the object.
◦ Active: Our country witnessed a terrible disaster.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "had witnessed" is the active form of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Simple Past Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "is witnessing" is the active form of the Present Continuous Tense, changing the time frame of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "witnesses" is the active form of the Simple Present Tense, again changing the tense of the original sentence.

NOTE

• When converting passive to active voice, the tense of the sentence must always be preserved — only the positions of the subject and object change, along with the form of the verb.

• Regular verbs like "witness" have identical Simple Past (V2) and Past Participle (V3) forms, which can make passive-to-active conversion in the Simple Past Tense look deceptively similar at first glance.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words/phrase.
Fail to notice; ignore; condone (an offence etc.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Overlook.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Overlook" means to fail to notice something, or to ignore or excuse an offence, mistake or fault. (अनदेखा करना / नज़रअंदाज़ करना)
◦ Example: The teacher decided to overlook his first mistake since it was an honest one.

• The word is formed from "over-" (beyond, above) + "look", originally meaning to look over or beyond something without noticing it closely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Overlong (बहुत लंबा): Excessively long in duration or length.

• Option 2: Overlie (के ऐनर लेटना): To lie on top of something, or (of a mother/animal) to accidentally smother a baby by lying on it.

• Option 3: Overly (अत्यधिक): Excessively; to too great a degree.

NOTE

• Other common one-word substitutes with "over-": Overhaul (thorough examination/repair), Overrule (reject a decision), Overrate (value too highly), Overt (open, not hidden).

• Do not confuse "Overlook" (to ignore/excuse) with "Look over" (to examine briefly) — the two have almost opposite shades of meaning in careful usage.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
He knows that / he has no other option / but to work hard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. but to work hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "but to work hard" contains the error. When the phrase "no other option/choice" is used, it must be followed by "than", not "but". The correct sentence should read: "He knows that he has no other option than to work hard."

• Rule:
◦ No option/choice + BUT + to-infinitive (without the word "other") — e.g., "He has no option but to resign."
◦ No other option/choice + THAN + to-infinitive (with the word "other") — e.g., "He has no other option than to resign."

• Since the given sentence already contains the word "other" ("no other option"), the following conjunction must be the comparative word "than", and not "but", which is used only when "other" is absent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "He knows that" is grammatically correct and introduces the noun clause that follows; it contains no error.

• Option 3: "he has no other option" is grammatically correct in itself — the word "other" is properly used here; the problem only arises in how the next segment connects to it.

• Option 4: "No error" is incorrect because the sentence does contain the "but/than" error identified above.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pairs in SSC error-spotting: "no sooner...than" (never "no sooner...when"), "scarcely...when/before" (never "scarcely...than"), and "other than" (never "other but").

• Remember: "but" in the sense of "except" pairs naturally with negative words like "no one," "nothing," "none" without "other"; as soon as "other" is added, the comparison word "than" must be used instead.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Cudgel one's brain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To think hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Cudgel one's brain(s)" means to think very hard about a problem, or to make a great mental effort to remember or solve something. (कड़ी मेहनत से सोचना / दिमाग पर ज़ोर डालना)
◦ Example: I cudgelled my brains all night but still couldn't solve the riddle.

• A "cudgel" is a short, thick stick used as a weapon; the idiom pictures someone figuratively "beating" their own brain to force out an idea or answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Thinking about a debate" is incorrect — the idiom is not restricted to debates; it refers to hard mental effort in general.

• Option 3: "Not to think" is incorrect — this is the opposite of the idiom's actual meaning.

• Option 4: "To overthink" is incorrect — overthinking implies excessive, often anxious, dwelling on something, whereas "cudgel one's brain" simply means making a strong deliberate effort to think.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to hard thinking often asked in SSC: "Rack one's brains" (to think very hard, a close synonym), "Put on one's thinking cap" (to think seriously about a problem), and "Beat one's brains out" (to try very hard to understand or solve something).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
When I was your age, I was working two jobs to provide for my family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No substitution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "to provide for" is already grammatically correct in the given sentence, so it needs no substitution.

• Rule: The infinitive of purpose ("to + base verb") is used to express the reason or purpose behind an action. Here, "to provide for" correctly expresses the purpose of working two jobs — i.e., in order to support the family financially.

• "Provide for someone" is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to supply someone with the money or things they need to live, and it is correctly used here in its to-infinitive form after the main verb "was working."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "to providing for" is incorrect because the infinitive marker "to" cannot be directly followed by the gerund ("-ing") form; "to" here must be followed by the base verb.

• Option 2: "for provide to" is incorrect because it disrupts the phrasal verb "provide for" and produces an ungrammatical sequence of words.

• Option 3: "on providing" is incorrect because the preposition "on" does not combine with "provide" to express purpose, and the gerund form is not appropriate after "was working" in this purposive sense.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "provide for" (to support financially/supply necessities) with "provide with" (to give something specific to someone), e.g., "The company provided him with a laptop."

• The infinitive of purpose can always be tested by expanding it mentally to "in order to" — "I was working two jobs (in order) to provide for my family" — if the sentence still makes sense, the to-infinitive is correctly used.

question: Select the sentence that contains no spelling errors.
option_1: The hippoputamus, also known as ‘river horse’, lives throughout sub Saharan Africa.
option_2: The hipopotamus, also known as ‘river horse’, lives throughout sub Saharan Africa.
option_3: The hippopotmaus, also known as ‘river horse’, lives throughout sub Saharan Africa.
option_4: The hippopotamus, also known as ‘river horse’, lives throughout sub Saharan Africa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The hippopotamus, also known as ‘river horse’, lives throughout sub Saharan Africa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "hippopotamus" — a large, thick-skinned, semi-aquatic mammal native to Africa, informally called the "river horse."
◦ Example: The hippopotamus spends most of the day submerged in rivers and lakes to keep cool.

• Spelling key: HIPPO + POTA + MUS. The word comes from Greek "hippos" (horse) + "potamos" (river), literally meaning "river horse." Note the double "p" in "hippo" and the sequence "p-o-t-a-m-u-s" that follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "hippoputamus" is incorrect; the letter "u" has wrongly replaced the "o" before "tamus."

• Option 2: "hipopotamus" is incorrect; one "p" has been dropped from "hippo," which should have a double "p."

• Option 3: "hippopotmaus" is incorrect; the letters "a" and "m" have been transposed near the end of the word.

NOTE

• The plural of "hippopotamus" can be either "hippopotamuses" or "hippopotami."

• Other Greek-origin animal names with tricky spellings frequently asked in SSC: rhinoceros, chimpanzee, chameleon and crocodile.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Bulk
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Handful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Bulk" means a large mass, quantity, or the majority of something. (बड़ी मात्रा / थोक)
◦ Example: The bulk of the company's profits comes from overseas sales.

• Its antonym, "Handful", means a small quantity or number of something — literally, as much as can be held in one hand. (मुठ्ठी भर / थोड़ी मात्रा)
◦ Example: Only a handful of students turned up for the extra class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Heavy (भारी): Of great weight; this describes a property related to bulk but is not its opposite in meaning.

• Option 3: Staple (मुख्य/प्रमुख): A main or principal item, especially of food or trade; unrelated in meaning to "bulk."

• Option 4: Brunt (मुख्य आघात): The chief impact or force of something unpleasant, e.g., "bore the brunt of the criticism"; not an antonym of "bulk."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Bulk": mass, volume, majority, magnitude.

• Other words meaning a small quantity, often tested as antonyms of "bulk" or "plenty": scarcity, dearth, paucity, and smattering.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She frankly confessed that she couldn't __________ to purchase a car then.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. afford.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "afford" means to have enough money, time, or resources to be able to do something, and it is typically followed by a to-infinitive, as in "can/can't afford to do something."

• Rule: The structure "could/couldn't + afford + to + verb" is used to talk about financial capability or incapability to do something. Here, the sentence needs a verb expressing that she lacked the financial means to purchase a car, which is exactly what "afford" conveys.

• Applying this: "She frankly confessed that she couldn't afford to purchase a car then" correctly conveys that she did not have enough money to buy a car.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "spend" is incorrect because "spend" means to pay out money one already has; it does not capture the idea of lacking sufficient means, and "couldn't spend to purchase" is not idiomatic.

• Option 3: "stand" is incorrect because "couldn't stand to purchase" would mean she couldn't tolerate/bear buying a car, which does not fit the context of financial confession.

• Option 4: "tolerate" is incorrect for the same reason as "stand" — it relates to endurance/patience, not financial capability, and does not fit naturally with "to purchase a car."

NOTE

• "Afford" is almost always used with "can/could" (usually in negative or question form) — "can afford," "can't afford," "could you afford."

• Do not confuse "afford" (to have enough money/resources) with "effort" (a noun meaning an attempt or exertion) — a common spelling/usage confusion in SSC exams.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
The natural environment is in contrast with the 'built environment' which refers to areas that have been fundamentally transformed and influenced by human activity, such as cities, towns, substructures and so on.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bipartisan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "influenced" means shaped, affected, or swayed by a particular factor or force — here, transformed one-sidedly by the effect of human activity. (प्रभावित)

• Its antonym in this context is "Bipartisan", which means representing or supported by two sides/parties equally, balanced and not swayed towards one particular influence. (निष्पक्ष / दोनों पक्षों से जुड़ा)
◦ Example: The committee's bipartisan approach ensured the decision was not influenced by any single group.

• Among the given options, "Bipartisan" best captures the sense of being free from one-sided influence, which is the opposite of "influenced."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Hackneyed (घिसा-पिटा): Overused and no longer interesting or effective due to repetition; unrelated to the idea of being influenced.

• Option 2: Inimical (प्रतिकूल): Harmful or hostile in effect; this describes a negative kind of influence rather than its opposite.

• Option 4: Interested (इच्छुक/स्वार्थी): Having a personal stake or concern in something; this is close in meaning to being "influenced" by self-interest rather than its opposite.

NOTE

• Related word pairs often tested in SSC: partisan (biased towards one side) ↔ impartial/bipartisan (unbiased, balanced).

• Other synonyms of "influenced": affected, swayed, shaped, moulded; other antonyms: unaffected, untouched, independent.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
The blind man said to me, “Can you help me cross the road?”
option_1: The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.
option_2: The blind man asked me if I will help him cross the road.
option_3: The blind man asked me if I could help him crossed the road.
option_4: The blind man asked me if I can help him cross the road.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is an interrogative sentence (a Yes/No question) in direct speech, using the modal "can."

• Rule — Narration of Yes/No questions:
◦ The reporting verb "said to" changes to "asked."
◦ Since there is no question word (what/where/why etc.), the conjunction "if" or "whether" is used to join the clauses.
◦ The interrogative structure of the direct question is changed to the assertive (statement) word order.
◦ The modal "can" changes to "could" in indirect speech, and pronouns change appropriately ("you"→"I", "me"→"him").

• Applying the rule: "Can you help me cross the road?" becomes "if I could help him cross the road."
◦ Indirect: The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "will" is not the correct backshifted form of "can"; the modal "can" must change to "could," not "will."

• Option 3 is incorrect because "crossed" wrongly changes the base verb "cross" into the past tense; after a modal like "could," the verb must remain in its base form ("cross"), not the past form.

• Option 4 is incorrect because the modal "can" has not been backshifted to "could" at all, which is required since the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense.

NOTE

• Modal backshift chart frequently tested in SSC: can → could, may → might, will → would, shall → should, must → had to/must.

• After any modal verb (could, would, should, might), the following main verb always stays in its base form (V1) — it is never inflected for tense.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
One has to be persistent in studies if he/she wants to get his/her dream job. Success will remain unattainable if one studies_________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. by fits and starts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic phrase "by fits and starts" means irregularly; in an inconsistent, stop-and-start manner, rather than steadily or continuously. (रुक-रुक कर / अनियमित रूप से)
◦ Example: He learnt to play the guitar by fits and starts, practising only when he felt like it.

• The sentence contrasts "persistent" (steady, continuous effort) with the opposite kind of effort that leads to failure — studying irregularly, i.e., "by fits and starts" — which logically explains why success "will remain unattainable."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "root and branch" (पूरी तरह से): Means thoroughly and completely; it does not fit the context of irregular effort leading to failure.

• Option 2: "the three R's" (शिक्षा के मूल तत्व): Refers to the basics of education — reading, writing and arithmetic; it does not describe a manner of studying.

• Option 3: "in ups and downs": This is not a standard idiomatic phrase in this form (the correct idiom is "to have its ups and downs"), and it does not fit grammatically or idiomatically in the blank.

NOTE

• Related idioms of irregularity often tested in SSC: "off and on" (occasionally), "now and then" (occasionally), and "in bits and pieces" (in small, disconnected parts).

• The opposite idea — steady, continuous effort — is expressed by phrases like "through thick and thin" or "day in and day out."

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A room where dead bodies are kept until burial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mortuary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Mortuary" means a room or building, especially in a hospital, where dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation. (शवगृह / मुर्दाघर)
◦ Example: The unidentified body was kept in the hospital mortuary for a week.

• The word comes from the Latin "mortuus", meaning "dead," the same root that gives us "mortal" and "mortality."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Sanatorium (स्वास्थ्यशाला): An establishment for the treatment of people who are convalescing or have chronic illnesses.

• Option 2: Museum (संग्रहालय): A building where objects of historical, artistic, or scientific interest are stored and exhibited.

• Option 4: Safari (जंगली यात्रा): An expedition to observe or hunt wild animals, especially in East Africa.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Mortuary" with "Cemetery" (a burial ground for the dead) or "Crematorium" (a place where dead bodies are cremated) — all three are commonly tested together in one-word substitution questions.

• Other "place"-related one-word substitutes frequently asked: Asylum (a place of refuge/shelter), Orphanage (home for children without parents), Armoury (a place where weapons are stored).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The important points were narrated in the class by the teacher.
option_1: The teacher was narrating important points in the class.
option_2: The teacher had narrated the important points in the class.
option_3: The teacher narrated the important points in the class.
option_4: In the class, the important points were narrated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The teacher narrated the important points in the class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The important points were narrated in the class by the teacher" is in the Simple Past Tense, Passive Voice.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the teacher" becomes the subject; the past participle "narrated" takes its simple past form "narrated"; and "the important points" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The teacher narrated the important points in the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was narrating" is the active form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had narrated" is the active form of the Past Perfect Tense, changing the tense of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it remains in the passive voice ("were narrated"), and therefore does not answer the question, which specifically asks for the active voice form.

NOTE

• While converting to active voice, the doer of the action (the agent introduced by "by") always becomes the subject of the new sentence, and the original subject becomes the object.

• Watch out for distractor options that either change the tense of the sentence or, as in Option 4 here, do not actually convert the voice at all.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She became frustrated with her poor health and began to lose _________ of her recovery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hope.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "to lose hope of something" means to stop believing or expecting that something good will happen, which fits the context of the sentence perfectly — being frustrated with poor health naturally leads to losing hope of recovering.

• Rule: The blank must be filled with a noun that logically collocates with "of her recovery" and connects sensibly with the earlier clause about becoming "frustrated." Only "hope" creates a meaningful, coherent sentence in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "weight" is incorrect because "lose weight of her recovery" is meaningless; "lose weight" is a fixed phrase but does not take "of + noun" in this sense.

• Option 2: "idea" is incorrect because "lose idea of her recovery" is not idiomatic or meaningful English.

• Option 3: "money" is incorrect because losing money has no logical connection with health or recovery in this context.

NOTE

• Common fixed collocations with "lose": lose hope (of), lose track (of), lose sight (of), lose faith (in), lose interest (in).

• The opposite phrase, "to hold on to hope" or "to keep hope alive," is often tested alongside "lose hope" in SSC vocabulary-in-context questions.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
She has / a habit of / spending against / her means.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. spending against.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "spending against" contains the error. The correct fixed expression is "to spend beyond one's means", not "spend against one's means." The sentence should read: "She has a habit of spending beyond her means."

• Rule: The idiomatic phrase "beyond one's means" means spending more money than one can afford, and it is the only preposition that correctly combines with "means" in this sense. "Against" does not carry this meaning and cannot be used here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "her means" is grammatically correct; "means" here correctly refers to financial resources.

• Option 2: "She has" is grammatically correct and properly introduces the sentence in the Simple Present Tense, agreeing with the singular subject "She."

• Option 4: "a habit of" is grammatically correct; "habit of" is correctly followed by a gerund phrase ("spending...").

NOTE

• Fixed idiomatic phrase: "to live beyond one's means" / "to spend beyond one's means" — meaning to spend more money than one earns or can afford.

• The opposite idea is expressed as "to live within one's means" — spending no more than what one can afford.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The action of damaging the good reputation of someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Defamation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Defamation" means the action of damaging the good reputation of someone, typically by making false or malicious statements about them. (मानहानि / चरित्र-हनन)
◦ Example: The newspaper was sued for defamation after publishing false allegations against the actor.

• The word is formed from the Latin "de-" (down, away) + "fama" (fame, reputation), literally meaning "to take away someone's fame/reputation."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Delegate (प्रतिनिधि): A person sent or authorised to represent others, especially at a conference; or, as a verb, to entrust a task to someone else.

• Option 2: Degeneration (अवनति): The process of becoming progressively worse in quality, character, or function.

• Option 4: Defection (दलबदल): The act of abandoning one's country, cause, or political party in favour of an opposing one.

NOTE

• Related legal one-word substitutes often asked in SSC: Libel (written defamation), Slander (spoken defamation), Perjury (lying under oath).

• Do not confuse "Defamation" (damaging reputation) with "Degeneration" (Option 2) — both begin with "De-" but have entirely different meanings.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
In December 2018
P. caused a landslide that
Q. an eruption of the volcano Anak Krakatau
R. triggered a tsunami in the Sunda Strait (Indonesia)
S. and killed more than 400 people
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QPRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is: "In December 2018 an eruption of the volcano Anak Krakatau (Q) caused a landslide that (P) triggered a tsunami in the Sunda Strait, Indonesia (R) and killed more than 400 people (S)."

• Rule: In para/sentence rearrangement, identify the grammatical subject that must directly follow the given opening phrase, and then trace the logical chain of cause and effect using the relative pronoun "that" and the conjunction "and."

• Applying this: the fixed opener "In December 2018" needs a subject to complete its clause, which is "Q" (an eruption of the volcano Anak Krakatau). This eruption is the subject that "P" (caused a landslide that) describes. The relative pronoun "that" in P needs a verb to complete the clause, given by "R" (triggered a tsunami...), and the tsunami's effect is completed by "S" (and killed more than 400 people), joined by "and."
◦ Order: Q → P → R → S

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: SQPR is incorrect because it begins with "and killed...", which cannot logically or grammatically follow the opening phrase "In December 2018."

• Option 2: RPQS is incorrect because it begins with "triggered a tsunami...", leaving no stated cause for the tsunami, and disrupts the cause-effect chain.

• Option 4: PRQS is incorrect because it begins with "caused a landslide that..." without ever stating what caused the landslide, making the sentence's opening incomplete and illogical.

NOTE

• In such rearrangement questions, always locate the segment that must immediately follow the fixed opening line — it usually contains the main grammatical subject.

• Trace connector words like "that," "and," "who," "which" carefully — they indicate which segment must directly follow another.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Loyal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fickle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Loyal" means faithful and steadfast in allegiance or support to a person, cause, or institution. (वफ़ादार / निष्ठावान)
◦ Example: The old servant remained loyal to the family for over thirty years.

• Its antonym, "Fickle", means changeable, inconstant, and likely to change one's loyalty, opinion, or affection without good reason. (चंचल / अस्थिर)
◦ Example: His fickle nature meant he switched allegiances every time it suited him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Ardent (उत्साही): Enthusiastic or passionate; this is actually closer in meaning to "loyal" (an ardent supporter) rather than being its opposite.

• Option 3: Stupid (मूर्ख): Lacking intelligence or common sense; unrelated in meaning to loyalty.

• Option 4: Tragic (दुखद): Causing or characterised by extreme distress or sorrow; unrelated in meaning to loyalty.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Loyal": faithful, devoted, staunch, steadfast.

• Other synonyms of "Fickle," often tested as antonyms of "loyal" or "constant": capricious, inconstant, flighty, and volatile.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
The dacoits ravaged the bungalow in the absence of its owner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Restored.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "ravaged" means severely damaged, devastated, or destroyed. (तबाह कर दिया / नष्ट कर दिया)
◦ Example: The cyclone ravaged the coastal villages, leaving nothing standing.

• Its antonym, "Restored", means brought back to a former good condition or state. (पुनर्स्थापित किया / फिर से ठीक कर दिया)
◦ Example: The old palace was carefully restored to its original grandeur.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Exploded (विस्फोट हुआ): Burst or blew up violently; while destructive, it is not the opposite of "ravaged" — it is closer in meaning.

• Option 2: Demolished (ध्वस्त किया): Pulled down or destroyed completely; this is a near-synonym of "ravaged," not its antonym.

• Option 4: Sealed (सील कर दिया): Closed off securely; this does not describe reversing damage and is unrelated to the meaning of "ravaged."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "ravaged": devastated, ransacked, plundered, wrecked.

• Other antonyms of "ravaged" that SSC may test: preserved, protected, safeguarded.

In the given passage, some words have been left out. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the pandemic, remote working has kept the work going on across _____ (1) Almost every industry got shut down physically during the lockdowns but the work from home model tried to ______ (2) the effect of the lockdown when it came to jobs. In the future also, many businesses across the globe, including the information technology industry, are ________ (3) continuing with the hybrid model. Remote working has replaced geography as a major hiring ________ (4), with 90 per cent of senior executives expected to work from home. As a result, 76 per cent of US organisations are more likely to _______ (5) out side the city or even state, according to a Talent Works poll of recruiting managers conducted across the US, quoted by an FE report.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sectors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that means distinct areas or branches of economic/industrial activity, since the next sentence refers to "every industry" being shut down. "Sectors" is the most natural collocation with "across" in this economic context — "across sectors" is a standard phrase meaning across different branches of the economy/industry.

• Rule: Word choice in cloze passages must be based on both grammatical fit and the most natural, idiomatic collocation used in standard English (especially in journalistic/formal writing, as this passage is), not merely a word that is loosely similar in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Fields" is a plausible near-synonym but is less precise here; "sectors" specifically refers to segments of the economy/industry, matching the following sentence about "every industry."

• Option 3: "Sections" does not collocate naturally with "across" in this economic/industrial sense; "sections" is more commonly used for parts of a document, organisation, or physical space.

• Option 4: "Areas" is too general and does not specifically convey the industry/economy-wide sense that the following sentence (about "every industry") requires.

NOTE

• Common collocations tested in SSC cloze passages: "across sectors," "across the board," "across the globe."

• When solving cloze passages, always read the sentence(s) immediately following the blank, since they often provide the clearest clue to the intended word.

In the future also, many businesses across the globe, including the information technology industry, are ________ (3) continuing with the hybrid model. Remote working has replaced geography as a major hiring ________ (4), with 90 per cent of senior executives expected to work from home. As a result, 76 per cent of US organisations are more likely to _______ (5) out side the city or even state, according to a Talent Works poll of recruiting managers conducted across the US, quoted by an FE report.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Reduce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word meaning to lessen or lower the impact of something, since the sentence talks about the work-from-home model responding to "the effect of the lockdown" on jobs. "Reduce" correctly conveys the idea of lessening this negative effect.

• Rule: In cloze passages, the chosen word must logically continue the cause-effect relationship of the sentence — here, remote working is presented as a solution that lessens (not increases, replaces or confirms) the negative impact of the lockdown on jobs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Substitute" does not fit because the work-from-home model did not "substitute the effect" of the lockdown — this phrase does not make logical sense in context.

• Option 3: "Replenish" means to fill up again or restock, which is unrelated to lessening a negative effect; it does not fit the context of the sentence at all.

• Option 4: "Substantiate" means to provide evidence to support a claim, which is unrelated to the idea of lessening the impact of the lockdown on jobs.

NOTE

• Common word confusions tested in cloze passages: "reduce" (lessen) vs. "replenish" (refill) vs. "substantiate" (prove) vs. "substitute" (replace).

• Always check whether the chosen word forms a logical cause-effect or purpose relationship with the rest of the sentence, not just a grammatically valid one.

During the pandemic, remote working has kept the work going on across _____ (1) Almost every industry got shut down physically during the lockdowns but the work from home model tried to ______ (2) the effect of the lockdown when it came to jobs. In the future also, many businesses across the globe, including the information technology industry, are ________ (3) continuing with the hybrid model. Remote working has replaced geography as a major hiring ________ (4), with 90 per cent of senior executives expected to work from home. As a result, 76 per cent of US organisations are more likely to _______ (5) out side the city or even state, according to a Talent Works poll of recruiting managers conducted across the US, quoted by an FE report.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Considering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word meaning thinking about or contemplating a course of future action, since the sentence discusses what businesses "in the future" plan to do — continue with the hybrid model. "Considering" correctly conveys businesses thinking about/planning to continue with this model.

• Rule: The correct word must fit the structure "are + [word] + continuing with the hybrid model" — grammatically, this requires a present participle that makes sense with "continuing" immediately after it, expressing an ongoing mental process about a future plan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Analysing" means examining something in detail to understand it; while businesses might analyse trends, "analysing continuing with the hybrid model" is not a natural or logical construction here.

• Option 2: "Examining" similarly means inspecting closely; it does not naturally combine with "continuing with" to express a future business plan.

• Option 4: "Observing" means watching or noticing something; it does not fit the sense of planning or intending a future course of action.

NOTE

• "Considering + gerund" (e.g., "considering continuing," "considering adopting") is a common structure in business/formal English to express that an option is being weighed for the future.

• Distinguish carefully between words describing mental evaluation ("considering," "contemplating") and words describing close inspection ("examining," "analysing," "observing") — cloze passages frequently test this distinction.

In the future also, many businesses across the globe, including the information technology industry, are ________ (3) continuing with the hybrid model. Remote working has replaced geography as a major hiring ________ (4), with 90 per cent of senior executives expected to work from home. As a result, 76 per cent of US organisations are more likely to _______ (5) out side the city or even state, according to a Talent Works poll of recruiting managers conducted across the US, quoted by an FE report.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Criterion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a singular noun meaning a standard or principle used for judging or deciding something, since it is preceded by the singular article "a" in the phrase "a major hiring ________." "Criterion" is the correct singular form of this word.

• Rule — Singular/Plural agreement: The Latin-origin noun "criterion" is singular, while "criteria" is its plural form. Since the blank follows the singular article "a" and the adjective "major," the singular form "criterion" must be used for grammatical agreement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Formula" does not fit the context — a formula is a fixed method or set of rules, not a standard/factor used in decision-making such as hiring.

• Option 2: "Standard" is close in general meaning but does not fit as naturally with "hiring" in this context as "criterion," which specifically means a factor used to judge or decide something (here, where to hire from).

• Option 3: "Criteria" is grammatically incorrect here because it is the plural form of "criterion," and it cannot follow the singular article "a."

NOTE

• Commonly confused singular-plural Latin/Greek noun pairs tested in SSC: criterion–criteria, phenomenon–phenomena, datum–data, medium–media, analysis–analyses.

• Always check the article and any preceding adjective before a blank — "a/an" or "this/that" signals a singular noun is required, while "these/those" or numbers greater than one signal a plural noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Implement" means to put a plan or decision into effect; it does not fit the idea of hiring people from outside the city or state.

• Option 2: "Deploy" means to move resources or personnel into position for a purpose, typically already-employed staff or equipment; it does not specifically convey the act of hiring new employees as "employ" does.

• Option 3: "Execute" means to carry out or perform a task or plan; it does not fit the context of hiring people from outside the city or state.

NOTE

• The passage's overall theme — recruiting managers, hiring criterion, senior executives working from home — consistently points to "employ" as the word most closely tied to recruitment/hiring vocabulary.

• Distinguish carefully between "employ" (to hire/give a job to someone) and "deploy" (to position/utilise resources that are already available) — a common confusion pair in SSC vocabulary-in-context questions.
